AROUND TOWN
Truck or Treat
RUTLAND — Wonderfeet Kids’ Museum will host its third annual Truck or Treat event Sunday, Oct. 19, on Merchants Row and Center Street in Rutland.
This combination “touch a truck” and “trick or treat” provides an opportunity to visit and explore interesting vehicles, while also taking part in a safe and supervised event. Last year’s event had over 80 sponsoring businesses with over 100 vehicles and drew over 4,000 visitors.
Trucks may be decorated for Halloween, participants to provide trick-or-treat candy, stickers or giveaways for as many as 4,000 kids. To register your vehicle, visit form.jotform.com/wonderfeetkidsmuseumvt/2025TruckOrTreatWKM. For more information, email WonderfeetEvents@wkmvt.org.
Carving contest
MANCHESTER — The Manchester Business Association and the Town of Manchester announce the return of the Pumpkin Carving Contest to be held Saturday, Oct. 18, immediately following the Harvest Day Celebration on Factory Point Green.
All ages are invited to showcase their carving skills and enter as many carved pumpkins as they’d like. Pre-registration is required and the online form can be found at manchestervermont.com/pumpkin-carving-contest. Each pumpkin must include a battery-operated light for nighttime viewing.
Drop off pumpkins from 10 a.m. to 3 p.m. Friday and Saturday, Oct. 17 and 18, at Manchester Visitor Center, 74 Depot St. Pumpkins will be on display at 5 p.m. Saturday and at noon Sunday, Oct. 19, along Depot Street in front of Factory Point Green. Prizes will be awarded in multiple age categories, as well as for the “Spookiest” and “Most Creative” pumpkin in each group. Winners will receive gift certificates to Union Underground, Charlie’s Coffee House, and Pastime Pinball.
Mask making
POULTNEY — Celebrate the Halloween season early with a Spooktacular Family Mask Making event from noon to 3 p.m. Sunday, Oct. 19, at Stone Valley Arts, 145 East Main St. Poultney. This drop-in program is free and open to local families.
In addition to making Halloween masks, edibles, including ginger “deadmen,” cauldron brownies, clementine pumpkins, boo berry bananas, graveyard dirt pudding and witch’s cider brew, will be served. There will also be Halloween-themed games like witch hat toss, ghost tin can bowling and a ghoulish photo booth.
Collaborative art
LUDLOW — Fletcher Farm recently received a $12,000 grant from Vermont Community Foundation to launch “Creating in Community,” a series of free monthly programs designed to bring neighbors together through collaborative art projects.
The first program will be held from 1 to 4 p.m. Sunday, Oct. 19, at Create Together at Fletcher Farm, 611 Route 103S. Ludlow. The initiative will continue on the third Sunday of each month, offering residents of all ages and experience levels the opportunity to learn new artistic techniques while working together on community-focused projects. Local artists and volunteers will assist Create Together staff in leading the workshops.
Since reopening in 2025 as a community art center, Create Together has focused on accessibility and affordability. The organization provides space, tools and instruction to come together and create, regardless of artistic background or financial circumstances. For more information, visit createtogethervt.org or call or text 802-228-8770.
Vocal concert
CHESTER — The First Universalist Parish of Chester (the Stone Church) will feature Big Woods Voices in concert at 4 p.m. Sunday, Oct. 19, 211 North St, Chester. Parking is on-site; the church is ADA accessible. Entry is by a sliding scale donation, $10-$20.
Big Woods Voices celebrates a cappella vocal harmony from multi-instrumental acoustic artist Will Danforth; area vocalist Alan Blood; Becky Graber, leader of Brattleboro Women’s Chorus and Good Trouble Street Choir; and Amanda Witman, Brattleboro Music Center faculty and co-leader of Brattleboro Pub Sing.
Public input
The Vermont Land Use Review Board will host four public engagement sessions across the state to get public input on draft Act 250 Tier 3 area rules and mapping.
All four meetings will be from 6 to 8 p.m. held in-person and remote. Remote connection information is available on the meeting agenda, at act250.vermont.gov/tier-3-rulemaking-and-report online.
Morrisville — Oct. 21, Morristown Tegu Building Meeting Room, 43 Portland St.
Rutland — Oct. 22, Regional Planning Commission Office, 16 Evelyn St. (2nd floor).
Newport — Oct. 28, City Gateway Center Meeting Room, 84 Fyfe Drive.
Windsor — Oct. 29, Select Board Meeting Room, 29 Union St.
While Act 250 jurisdiction is shrinking in downtown and village centers (Tier 1 areas), it is expanding in critical natural resource areas (Tier 3 areas). The Tier 3 rules and mapping will determine development requires an Act 250 permit in these critical natural resource areas.
Questions and comments can be submitted any time by email at act250.rulemaking@vermont.gov.
MILITARY NEWS
Writers’ symposium
NORTHFIELD — Norwich University will host the 2025 Military Writers’
Symposium, titled “The Shadow Front: Unconventional Approaches to Warfare,” Oct. 27-28 on its Northfield campus.
Open to the public, this year’s theme explore often hidden dimensions of conflict where traditional rules of engagement are abandoned in favor of subversion, innovation and psychological manipulation.
The symposium will also feature the presentation of the 2025 William E. Colby Award to Simon Shuster, senior correspondent at TIME.
For more information, visit the Norwich University website.
AROUND VT
Protect clean water
As winter approaches, the Department of Environmental Conservation wants to remind construction professionals and property owners about additional requirements to help protect state waterways during the winter construction season. Wintertime rainfall, thaws and snowmelt can produce significant flows over frozen and saturated ground. These flows can then increase erosion and sediment flow. To learn more, view the permit application instructions or the Low Risk Site Handbook.
